newsitem.title: USA: California ordered to hire welfare recipients.
newsitem.headline: California ordered to hire welfare recipients.

text.p: California Governor Pete Wilson on Friday ordered state agencies and departments to hire more welfare recipients.

Wilson's executive order directs all state agencies, departments, boards and commissions "to maximise the employment of welfare recipients," and to ensure they have the opportunity to compete for state jobs.
In January, the Republican governor unveiled his welfare reform plans. In line with federal reforms, Wilson's plan sets a state lifetime limit of five years on aid.

But under his plan, starting from 1998, able-bodied people currently on welfare may only receive aid for a total of 24 months during any 36-month period. New recipients may only receive aid for 12 months during any 24 month period.
Democratic legislators have criticised Wilson's plan, accusing him of not doing enough to find jobs for welfare recipients who will be cut off from aid.
